what: NV's predictions and decision rules (DESIGN.md §3 and §5). Fixed before the first card write: `freeze.sh --predictions` writes PREDICTIONS.sha256 over this file, every real block refuses unless it checks, and the validation freeze checks it again. Development may change nv.json's timing_s, limits, heater and analysis fields, never this file; a change here after PREDICTIONS.sha256 exists is an amendment, dated before any data it touches.

NV-I.what: decided on the idle rail corrected to the pass's 485 mV idle die temperature; TH-LEAK passes when the interval lies inside [1.0, 3.5] (the current rises with the voltage); where the interval sits against 1.25 (constant-current-like below, leakage-like above) is descriptive

nv_i_temp_coef_source: E44 cooling, 485 mV, whole-degree bins, d ln(noc_w)/dT: aifoundry3 2.69-2.86 %/C (54-84 C), aifoundry2 2.74-2.83 %/C (67-83 C), aifoundry1-c1 2.73-2.92 %/C; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/raw/<card>/idle/p1-3

e42_reference_fj_per_bit_hop.what: mesh rail, wsep d1-4, median of E42's six passes per card (docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/raw/<card>/wire), recomputed with analyze_wire.bursts()

c_meter.what: per pass, the least-squares slope of the 12 V board idle power on the mesh-rail idle power across the pass's levels, both corrected to the pass's 485 mV idle die temperature (board: analyze_wire's leakage law; rail: nv_i_temp_coef_per_c); a true rail meter gives 1/efficiency, a meter that multiplies the current by a fixed voltage about 2.1-2.8. A pass contributes only if its temperature-corrected rail idle rose by min_rise_w or more from 485 to 600 mV; if most valid passes' rail did not rise, C-METER is NOT APPLICABLE (the reading does not follow the rail) and only the zero theories (TH-0, TH-DI-0, TH-I-0) can be decided

val_passes_rule.what: N, the validation passes, is the smallest number with t(0.975, N-1) * SD_dev / sqrt(N) <= target_half_width, SD_dev the development per-pass SD of n_D; at least min; if more than max would be needed the design is revisited before any validation pass (an amendment)

r1.rule: the 95% Welch interval of n_D(validation) - n_D(development) lies inside [-tol, +tol]; FAIL when it lies wholly outside
